edges.description: Establishes oxidative stress and mitochondrial structural defects in human motor neurons carrying a GDAP1 mutation, the cell type the disease affects.
edges.limitations: The patient carries a homozygous premature-termination-codon allele (c.581C>G, p.Ser194*) degraded by nonsense-mediated decay — a loss-of-function, recessive genotype, and the paper describes the patient as CMT2H. It therefore cannot report on the dominant fusion-interference mechanism curated here, and supports only the shared downstream oxidative and mitochondrial endpoint. Notably ATP production was preserved, so the bioenergetic component of this node is not reproduced.
edges.source: hiPSC-derived motor neurons from a GDAP1 patient

edges.description: Reproduces the axonal neuropathy endpoint of GDAP1 disease in vivo, with motor neuron loss and neuromuscular junction pathology.
edges.limitations: This is a null allele, so it models the loss-of-function lesion that underlies recessive GDAP1 neuropathy, not the dominant CMT2K mechanism. Recessive alleles reduce fission activity whereas dominant alleles interfere with fusion and raise ROS, so the knockout cannot report on the mechanism curated for this entry — it supports the shared downstream axonal endpoint only. The paper itself frames its findings as relevant to the axonal recessive form.

nodes.description: The distal-to-proximal gradient of axonal loss produces distal weakness and wasting with milder sensory involvement and foot deformity, beginning in the lower limbs. Reflexes are not uniformly lost: generalized areflexia is reported in a severe dominant case, while a mild heterozygous series found normal reflexes in four of five subjects.

evidence.reference_title: Similar clinical, pathological, and genetic features in Chinese patients with autosomal recessive and dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2K.
evidence.snippet: All patients had disease onset before 5 years of age, and presented with muscle weakness, atrophy, and mild sensory disturbance in distal limbs.

nodes.description: Dominant CMT2K alleles are overwhelmingly missense changes in the GST-like core of GDAP1. Crystallographic and biophysical work on the dominant variants H123R (a Finnish founder allele) and R120W shows that the mutant proteins fold and behave in solution much like wild type but are markedly less thermally stable, with the substitutions disrupting a side-chain interaction network linking helices alpha-3, alpha-6 and alpha-7. The lesion is therefore a destabilised but still-assembled protein rather than an absent one. Note that thermal destabilization does not by itself explain dominance: the same structural work finds it in recessive alleles too, so what makes these alleles dominant is not established at the protein level and is inferred from the cellular phenotype instead.

evidence.reference_title: Structural insights into Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-linked mutations in human GDAP1.
evidence.snippet: The disease variant proteins retain close to normal structure and solution behavior, but both present a significant decrease in thermal stability.

evidence.reference_title: Conserved intramolecular networks in GDAP1 are closely connected to CMT-linked mutations and protein stability.
evidence.snippet: All disease variant proteins retain close to normal structure and solution behaviour.

evidence.reference_title: Structural insights into Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease-linked mutations in human GDAP1.
evidence.snippet: Here, we describe the biochemical and structural properties of the Finnish founding CMT2K mutation H123R and CMT2K-linked R120W, both of which are autosomal dominant mutations.

nodes.description: A constitutive Gdap1 knockout mouse with abnormal motor behaviour from about three months, electrophysiologically and biochemically confirmed axonal neuropathy, progressive anterior horn motor neuron loss, neuromuscular junction defects, and, in cultured motor and dorsal root ganglion neurons, large defective mitochondria, altered ER cisternae, reduced alpha-tubulin acetylation, increased autophagy vesicles, and a blunted store-operated calcium entry response.

Wild-type GDAP1 is a mitochondrial fission factor that acts through Drp1 and Fis1. The dominant CMT2K alleles do not simply reduce that fission activity — which is what the recessive alleles do — but instead interfere with mitochondrial fusion, producing an unbalanced and abnormally distributed mitochondrial network. This inheritance-dependent split is the central mechanistic distinction between CMT2K and recessive GDAP1 neuropathy.

evidence.reference_title: GDAP1 mutations differ in their effects on mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis depending on the mode of inheritance.
evidence.snippet: Recessively inherited CMT-associated forms of GDAP1 (rmGDAP1s) have reduced fission activity, whereas dominantly inherited forms (dmGDAP1s) interfere with mitochondrial fusion.

evidence.reference_title: GDAP1 mutations differ in their effects on mitochondrial dynamics and apoptosis depending on the mode of inheritance.
evidence.snippet: we demonstrate that GDAP1 is a mitochondrial fission factor whose activity is dependent on the fission factors Drp1 and Fis1

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypical features of a new dominant GDAP1 pathogenic variant (p.R226del) in axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Transfection of HeLa cells with the p.R226del mutation led to an increased mitochondrial aggregation.

nodes.description: Long peripheral axons depend on mitochondria trafficked over great distances, so a mitochondrial network that is poorly distributed and bioenergetically compromised fails first at the distal ends of the longest fibres. Sural nerve biopsy in CMT2K shows loss of large myelinated fibres with regeneration clusters, and electron microscopy shows mitochondrial aggregation in axons and Schwann cells with neurofilament accumulation.

evidence.snippet: Electron microscopy showed mitochondrial aggregation in both axons and Schwann cells, and neurofilament accumulation in giant unmyelinated fibers.

evidence.reference_title: Similar clinical, pathological, and genetic features in Chinese patients with autosomal recessive and dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2K.
evidence.snippet: Sural nerve biopsy revealed loss of large myelinated fibers with regeneration clusters and a few onion bulbs.

nodes.description: There is no disease-modifying therapy. Management is symptomatic and rehabilitative, delivered by a team spanning neurology, physiatry, orthopedic surgery, and physical and occupational therapy, and includes daily heel cord stretching to prevent Achilles shortening, ankle-foot orthoses, walking aids, and analgesia for musculoskeletal pain.

evidence.snippet: Treatment is symptomatic and involves evaluation and management by a multidisciplinary team that includes neurologists, physiatrists, orthopedic surgeons, and physical and occupational therapists.

evidence.snippet: Treatment may include: daily heel cord stretching exercises to prevent Achilles tendon shortening, ankle/foot orthoses, orthopedic surgery, forearm crutches or canes, wheelchairs, treatment of musculoskeletal pain with acetaminophen or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory agents, and career and employment counseling.

nodes.description: Dominant GDAP1 alleles raise reactive oxygen species production and give uneven mitochondrial transmembrane potentials. In patient fibroblasts the severity of this redox lesion tracks the affected protein domain: p.C240Y, inside the GST domain, carries a mitochondrial complex I defect with greater oxidative stress and faster clinical progression than p.R120W outside it. Downstream of complex I deficiency the redox-sensitive deacetylase SIRT1 and its target NRF1 are both reduced.

evidence.reference_title: Oxidative stress contributes differentially to the pathophysiology of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2K.
evidence.snippet: We show that complex I deficiency leads to a redox potential alteration and a significant reduction of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression, a major deacetylase sensitive to the cellular redox state, and NRF1 the downstream target of SIRT1.

evidence.reference_title: Oxidative stress contributes differentially to the pathophysiology of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 2K.
evidence.snippet: The CMT2K axonal form is associated with GDAP1 dominant mutations, which according to the affected domain cause a gradient of severity.

nodes.description: Human induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived motor neurons from a GDAP1 patient and normal controls. GDAP1 mRNA is mainly expressed in motor neurons in normal subjects and is drastically reduced in the patient's cells. Patient motor neurons show reduced viability with lipid dysfunction and oxidative stress, and mitochondrial cristae defects without an ATP production deficit.
